newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia ruling Golkar party favours Suharto.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia ruling Golkar party favours Suharto.

text.p: Indonesia's ruling Golkar political party stopped short of nominating President Suharto as its 1998 presidential candidate but said age was not a factor in choosing a candidate.

Golkar party chairman Harmoko (Eds: one word) said at the end of the party's three-day annual congress on Friday that any future president should have a vision of how to unite the nation but that age was not a consideration.
"We will not include any age restriction (in our choice)," Harmoko said.
Harmoko refused to confirm that Golkar would support 75-year old Suharto's re-election but said that the incumbent president was still "the nation's best leader".
Golkar will formally announce its presidential candidate in March 1998 at the meeting of the People's Consultative Assembly, the body which nominates Indonesia's president, Harmoko said.
Suharto, who took effective control of the country after an abortive communist coup in 1965, has won six five-year terms unopposed and is widely expected to run for a seventh term in 1998.

Golkar, which celebrates its 32nd anniversary tomorrow, said last week that it hopes to increase its share of the vote to 71 percent in next year's parliamentary elections, after obtaining 68 percent in 1992.
